archive.name: Nora Hart
archive.intro: Nora ran the town library for forty years and never once returned a book late.
archive.why: Because the little ones only knew her as a name on a shelf plaque.

chapters.title: The library years
chapters.description: 1958 to 1998, behind the same oak desk.

detailCards.label: What she always said
detailCards.value: "A book is never late if it comes back loved."

stories.title: The night she kept the library open
stories.body: The blizzard closed everything but her. She lit the reading lamps and let half the street sleep in the stacks.

stories.title: On patience
stories.body: "Nothing worth reading was written in a hurry, and nothing worth doing either."

recipes.title: Nonie's brown-butter shortbread
recipes.body: Brown a half pound of butter until it smells like toast. Two cups flour, half a cup sugar, a pinch of salt. Press into the tin with the back of a spoon — she said hands make it tough. Score before baking, 325 until the edges go gold.

timeline.title: Became head librarian at Millbrook
timeline.desc: Youngest head librarian the town had ever appointed.

letters.author: June Hart
letters.title: The card catalog of her heart
letters.body: If you ever wonder whether she would have liked you: she kept a shelf for every kind of person who walked in.

photos.caption: Nora at the oak desk, stamp in hand, 1983.

thingsLoved.title: The smell of new paperbacks
thingsLoved.why: She opened every delivery box like a birthday present.

readme:
# Nora Hart — archive export

This is a complete, open export of a DearestEllie family archive, in the
Open Memory Format (files named .omf.json / .omf.zip).
It is yours to keep, read, and move anywhere. No part of it depends on us.

- Format version: 1.1
- Format specification: https://github.com/DearestEllie/open-memory-format
- Generated: 2026-07-10T09:30:00.000Z

Open the .json file in any text editor, or load it with any JSON tool.
Every section is a plain array of records. Dates are kept as written —
an approximate year stays approximate; nothing was invented.
